jobs._command: COMMAND JOB since 2026-10-12 (DPLAN-0405, devpulse ruling 2; FPLAN-9994 phase 1): the daemon tick runs the verb as a subprocess from src/aipass/seedgo/, so no sonnet wake, no background-and-poll, no tokens. The verb still emails its own one-screen summary to @devpulse, so notify is false (daemon's notify.email would add a start and a finish mail on top). Phase 4 moves the Sunday mail to the ratchet and adds --no-mail here. Timeout 1800: measured 2 min warm, 6 min cold; a command job holds the tick lock for its whole run. The runstate row's next_run is 2026-10-18T03:56 - the week drifted from 03:00 to 03:56 when the old wake fired late, and interval counts from last_run.
jobs._slot: Intended slot: Sunday 03:00 local, and the `slot` field above now says so in the file itself (@daemon shipped it 2026-09-07 on this branch's design point, FPLAN-0492 ruling 6). An interval job otherwise has no time field - it fires on the first daemon tick after it is enabled and then every 10080 minutes from that moment - so before `slot` existed the slot was set by SEEDING last_run and nothing in this file recorded it. A slot is one ISO instant naming ONE occurrence of the rhythm; a job that has never run is seeded from it, and a past slot is rolled forward by whole intervals rather than used verbatim, so the line above stays correct however long it sits here. Sunday 03:00 is the quiet window: no human at the keyboard, no PR train, and clear of @daemon's own 09:00 inbox-sweep. The cycle saturates the CPU for its whole run (pyright per branch, one git blame per test file) and it evicts the aipass-pack audit cache, so the next interactive 'audit aipass' is a cold full scan - both are reasons it must not land during a working session.
jobs._note: ENABLED 2026-09-07 01:39 on the owner's ruling (01:16, relayed by devpulse in FPLAN-0491: seal DPLAN-0323, switch the weekly v5 cadence on). SLOT SEEDED by @daemon at 01:48 the same night: daemon_json/daemon_runstate.json carries last_run 2026-09-06T03:00:00 and next_run 2026-09-13T03:00:00, so the 10080-minute week counts from Sunday 03:00 as intended. @daemon verified it against is_job_due() at six instants rather than by eye; the Sunday 03:00 boundary is exact because interval measures from last_run, not from last success. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN BETWEEN, recorded because it was luck and not a guard: the job tried to fire TWICE before the seed landed - @daemon's logs/run.log lines 61-62, 01:34:52 and 01:40:20, both 'Blocked firing @seedgo/shadow-cycle-weekly: lock: Active agent (PID 432478)'. The only thing that stopped the week locking to 01:34 Monday was that seedgo happened to be awake in its own branch holding that lock. record_job_blocked leaves last_run alone on purpose, so _is_interval_due kept answering True on every tick and the sole brake was _in_blocked_hold's five minutes. SEED FIRST, THEN ENABLE - OR DECLARE A SLOT, which is the same ordering written down once instead of remembered: @daemon seeds from an ABSENT last_run rather than an absent runstate row, precisely so a job carrying a blocked row with no last_run - this one, that night - is still seeded. If this row is ever pruned or the runstate rebuilt, the slot re-seeds it instead of locking the week to whatever minute the next tick landed on.

WHAT: the execution ratchet (DPLAN-0405, FPLAN-9994 phase 1). Picks the branch probed least recently from .seedgo/ratchet_series.jsonl, runs audit-tests --pseudo-tested on it under a 1800 s campaign budget, archives the artifact to .seedgo/ratchet/ and appends one series line. Every probe writes its line. A not_applicable week (the target could not be measured, the reason in the line) exits 0; a campaign that ran out of budget exits 6 and its branch is picked again next week, continuing from the first unprobed function (slice k/N), so ok_exit_codes [6] makes that week a pass in @daemon's finish mail. Only a lane that could not run exits non-zero otherwise (2), so this job reads FAILED only then. WHEN: Sunday 04:00, behind shadow-cycle-weekly (next_run 03:56): ticks serialise under tick_lock and due jobs fire in file order, so the two never overlap. It holds the tick for up to 3600 s, so @prax's Sunday 04:00 tmp sweep and 04:30 module scan fire on the first tick after it. WHY notify.email: phase 1 sends no mail of its own; daemon's finish mail to @devpulse carries the exit code and the output tail until phase 4's Sunday mail lands. Phase 2 adds the hand-off dispatch to the probed branch's owner.
